t.7.86.1: For many days Rāma listened to that most wondrous song, together with the sages, the kings and the monkeys.
t.7.86.2: When that song had been sung, Rāma, having recognized Kuśa and Lava as the two sons of Sītā, spoke these words in the midst of that assembly.
t.7.86.3: "Go into the presence of the blessed one and speak my words to him."
t.7.86.4: If she is pure in her conduct, if indeed she is free from sin, let her, having obtained the consent of the great sage, here give proof of her own purity.
t.7.86.5: Having learned the wish of the sage and the inner mind of Sītā, who desires to give proof, then report to me quickly.
t.7.86.6: Tomorrow at daybreak, let Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, take an oath here in the midst of the assembly, for the sake of my purification as well.
t.7.86.7: Having heard these most wonderful words of Rāghava, the messengers set out together for the enclosure where the bull among sages was dwelling.
t.7.86.8: Having bowed to that great-souled one, blazing and of boundless splendor, they spoke to him Rāma's words, gentle and sweet.
t.7.86.9: Having heard those words of theirs and having understood what was in Rāma's mind, the sage of very great splendour then spoke these words.
t.7.86.10: So be it, blessings be upon you; Sītā will do whatever pleases Rāghava, for a husband is a woman's deity.
t.7.86.11: Thus addressed by the sage, all the messengers of Rāma, men of great vigor, returned to Rāghava, and all of them reported the words of the sage.
t.7.86.12: Then Kākutstha, filled with joy on hearing the words of the great-souled one, addressed the sages and the kings who had assembled there.
t.7.86.13: Let the revered ones together with their disciples, and the kings with their retinues, and whoever else so desires, witness the oath of Sītā.
t.7.86.14: Having heard those words of the great-souled Rāghava, a great cry of "Well done!" arose from all the foremost of the sages.
t.7.86.15: And the great-souled kings praised Rāghava: "O best of men, this is fitting in you alone on earth, and in no one else."
t.7.86.16: Having thus made the decision that it would take place on the morrow, Rāghava, the slayer of foes, then dismissed them all.
